exposure: Underlying etiological factors (traumatic brain injuries, metabolic disorders, neurovascular diseases)
outcome: MRI-detected structural brain abnormalities (periventricular leukomalacia, cerebral atrophy, schizencephaly)
cohort: The study included 65 pediatric patients, aged 1 month to 15 years, with developmental delay, excluding those with previously confirmed genetic syndromes or metabolic disorders.
finding: MRI identified structural brain abnormalities in 76.9% of children with developmental delay, with periventricular leukomalacia, cerebral atrophy, and schizencephaly being most common, and these abnormalities were significantly associated with developmental delays alongside strong correlations with hypoxic insults, traumatic brain injuries, metabolic disorders, and neurovascular diseases.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery had no significant association with structural brain abnormalities (p = 0.164).
cross-section timing: Enrollment and assessment were performed from October 2024 to January 2025.
